name: Escape Routes from Direct-Measure Barriers for Duplicating Recursion
description: Shows every successful orienter lies outside enumerated universes via the third disjunct. Every duplicating family admits one-way classification and three exact escape routes.

program.name: The Termination Axis
program.summary: The rule recΔ b s (δ n) → app s (recΔ b s n) copies its payload and consumes one counter; a direct measure orients it exactly when it ignores the payload and increases strictly with the counter, and the additive, affine, matrix, arctic, tropical and Knuth-Bendix families fail under their stated premises, with mutual cycles and higher-order sharing as variants. The proofs that succeed change the observer: the dependency-pair projection to the counter, nonlinear coupling, and the lexicographic and multiset path orders; seventy-six methods and a residual catalog record the verdicts as bookkeeping.

oneLine: Every direct orienter of the KO7 root relation fails wrapper-subterm sensitivity, base transparency or membership in the enumerated barrier universes, and in fact leaves those universes; every observer that orients a duplicating recursive family fails strict exposure, unbounded pump, visibility or sensitivity at each payload coordinate; and every KO7 orienter lands in one of three escape routes.
summary: The theory studies right-duplicating recursor schemas with one left and at least two right occurrences of a distinguished payload, duplicating recursive families adding step, pump and exposure data, and explicit KO7 direct-orienter universes with tracked primary scalars and enumerated barrier universes. The questions are global orientation of the duplicating step by a direct measure, the enumerated families such an orienter can belong to, and the escape routes that remain. Any orienter that globally orients lies outside the Nat, extended, pump-free and projection barrier universes, so each trichotomy holds through its third disjunct of failed sensitivity, failed transparency or non-representability. The extended barrier universe is the union of disjoint scalar and structural halves, neither of which orients, and KO7 orientation is equivalent to orientation packaged with a concrete escape clause. An observer that orients a duplicating family fails exposure, pump, visibility or sensitivity at each payload coordinate, every orienting KO7 observer lands in one of three routes (projection or dependency pairs, nonlinear outside the class, ablation), the distinguished payload count rises strictly with gap at least one, arctic matrix families with finite wrapper diagonals are blocked, and catalog rows project onto existing theorem-backed surfaces. The schema-level outside-boundary theorem states, for all KO7 base and step traces, that every uniform-cost direct measure gives the KO7 recursor orbit linearly growing mass; its schema argument is unused, so it carries no information about the schema. Conditions include global-orientation hypotheses, wrap-diagonal finiteness or positivity for matrix families, and no-sharing or freshness for higher-order lifts.
boundary: Inside the enumerated direct-barrier universes no measure globally orients the KO7 duplicating step, so a global orientation gives up wrapper-subterm sensitivity, base transparency or representability, and the universe splits into disjoint scalar and structural halves, each without an orienter. For a duplicating recursive family the distinguished payload count rises strictly with gap at least one, and an orienting observer escapes by failure of exposure, pump, visibility or sensitivity; the implication runs one way, from orientation to escape. The schema-level outside-boundary theorem concerns KO7 recursor orbits under uniform-cost direct measures and makes no use of the schema.

conclusions.statement: For every Nat-valued measure mu, if mu globally orients with less-than then mu is not in the Nat-valued barrier universe.
For every direct orienter O, if O orients then its primary scalar is not wrapper-subterm sensitive or not transparent at base or O is not representable in the extended barrier universe.

For every Nat-valued measure mu, if mu globally orients with less-than then mu is not wrapper-subterm sensitive on the KO7 schema or not transparent at base on the KO7 schema or not pump-free Nat representable.

For every duplicating system Sys and every Nat-valued measure mu on its terms, if mu globally orients Sys with less-than then mu is not wrapper-subterm sensitive or not transparent at base or not Nat representable for that schema.
For every duplicating recursive family F, every direct whole-term observer O and every payload coordinate i, if O globally orients F then O falls into the four-clause escape disjunction at i.
For every duplicating recursive family F, the packaged schema-generic one-way escape characterization holds.
For every KO7 direct orienter O, if O orients then O yields a recursive-family escape witness in one of the three routes.
For every explicit KO7 observer O, O orients exactly when O is an escaping orienter packaging orientation with an escape clause.
For every orienter O, extended representability holds exactly when scalar representability or structural representability holds.
For every orienter O, if O is scalar-barrier representable then O does not orient.
For every orienter O, if O is structural-barrier representable then O does not orient.

For every right-duplicating recursor schema S and all KO7 traces b and s, every uniform-cost direct measure gives the KO7 recursor orbit from b and s a mass affine in the counter depth; the embedding ignores S, so the statement carries no information about the schema.
For a duplicating recursive family F, the distinguished payload count of the left-hand side is strictly less than that of the right-hand side.
For any duplicating schema S, dimension d, arctic matrix measure M and coordinate i, if M is wrap-diagonal-finite at i then there is no universal ArcticLt orientation of the duplicating step at i.
For every recursive-family boundary closeout row, its projection proposition onto the existing substrate surface holds.

openPoints: Nothing is claimed about methods outside the explicit direct-orienter universes, and the first two trichotomy disjuncts add no information beyond the third.
No converse is claimed beyond the formalized class; the schema-generic one-way map has its converse only at KO7.
Higher-order tree lifts need a no-sharing hypothesis and full-capture avoidance needs body freshness, while innermost-only and AC-quotient scopes lie outside the barrier scope.
Closed firability is metadata only, and raw trace counting cannot separate roles under repeated instantiation so role-aware counting is required.
Exposure stays abstract and is tied to payload-count rise only by certificate, and the W2 transformed-call route carries no certified dependency-pair processor claim.

files.summary: The file wraps a right-duplicating recursor schema with a step relation and witnesses for the rule step, pump and exposure. It keeps exposure abstract but ties it to a payload-count rise by certificate. It forwards the distinguished coordinate and gap. It proves the distinguished count strictly rises and the gap is at least one.
files.conclusion: The family packages the schema with step, pump and exposure data and lifts the strict payload-count rise and gap of at least one.

files.summary: The file projects each of the five licensed-method data into existentials or unchanged negative propositions without manufacturing witnesses. It passes through the canonical sensitivity and transparency failures. It re-exports the trichotomy negatives and represented-barrier incompatibility. It shows every route disposition is supported because missing structure is uninhabited.
files.conclusion: Every licensed method projects to its success datum unchanged and every route disposition lands supported because missing structure is empty.

files.summary: The file splits the fourteen-constructor representability predicate into scalar and structural halves. It proves the exact partition equivalence and derived disjointness. It proves orientation incompatible with each half separately. It retains the three-way direct theorem and its refined restatement. It defines a five-tag route catalog with a licensed universe inhabited everywhere, empty missing structure and computed supported counts.
files.conclusion: The represented barrier splits exactly into disjoint scalar and structural halves that never orient, while the retained three-way theorem stays universal and all five positive routes are licensed and supported.

files.summary: The file defines an explicit KO7 direct-orienter universe with scalar and tracked-primary orders and primary-scalar projection. It proves every successful Nat-valued and extended orienter lies outside its enumerated barrier universe. Each escape trichotomy therefore holds via its third disjunct. It adds a projection layer and derives weighted-functional and mixed-coordinate matrix corollaries.
files.conclusion: Every successful direct, extended or projected orienter lies outside its enumerated universe, so each trichotomy holds via its third disjunct.

files.summary: The file extends the pump-free escape trichotomy with four added families and records a verdict for each. Finite-diagonal arctic matrices are blocked while a bottom-diagonal arctic member strictly orients, so the arctic family is split. The tropical family escapes with a compiled min-plus orienter, and the unconstrained direct law and textbook duplicating rule are blocked. It separately packages the five TTT2 MAYBE rows, giving universal obstructions for POLY, KBO, MAT(2) and MAT(3) and keeping the no-linear-bound fact as an independent invariant rather than an FBI explanation.
files.conclusion: Every added family carries its exact verdict, with the arctic family split, the tropical family escaping, the other two blocked, and the TTT2 rows separated into four obstructions plus an independent invariant.

files.summary: The file restates both KO7 escape trichotomies over pump-free universes with growth premises discharged. It defines a Nat-valued representability predicate and an extended orienter universe with tracked vector readings, and proves that global orientation forces failure of wrapper-subterm sensitivity, base transparency, or representability. It proves the pump-free Nat universe contains the pumped universe by forgetting pump fields.
files.conclusion: Both trichotomies hold over the pump-free universes, and every pumped representable measure is pump-free representable.

files.summary: The file isolates the schema-generic part of the escape trichotomy. It defines wrapper-subterm sensitivity, base transparency, and Nat-valued direct representability over a duplicating schema. It proves that global orientation of a system implies failure of one of those three properties.
files.conclusion: Global orientation implies failure of sensitivity, transparency, or representability for any duplicating system.

files.summary: This file gives the KO7-instantiated half of the escape-route characterization. It defines five concrete escape clauses and packaged escaping orienters, proves forward coverage from the escape trichotomy and a backward projection, combines them into an iff on the explicit KO7DirectOrienter universe, and closes it together with the schema-generic theorem.
files.conclusion: An explicit KO7 direct observer orients KO7 exactly when it packages orientation with one of five concrete escape clauses.

files.summary: This file adds a role-aware KO7 adapter with formal b, s and n role variables so the payload can be counted exactly. It defines occurrence predicates, counts, left and right terms with counts one and two, and projection to Trace. It packages KO7 as a right-duplicating recursor schema and proves every closed instance projects to a live kernel rec_succ step.
files.conclusion: KO7 is a right-duplicating recursor schema whose role-aware sides project onto live kernel rec_succ steps.

files.summary: This file is a surface layer cataloguing eleven recursive-family boundary deliverables as a finite row inventory. It records per-row projection witnesses onto existing theorem-backed substrate identifiers without asserting new schema content. It proves the catalog has length eleven without duplicates and is complete, and that every projection holds by reusing substrate theorems. It closes with a phase-G marker conjoining completeness and projection.
files.conclusion: All eleven recursive-family boundary rows project onto existing theorem-backed substrate identifiers with an exact complete catalog.

files.summary: This file packages the recursive-family escape surface into one review-facing certificate. It defines a packed structure covering the unconditional boundary, boundary-catalog size and witnesses, the exact three-row escape inventory and lift, and generic plus KO7 escape characterization. It proves the certificate by aggregation over already-landed modules and adds no new mathematics.
files.conclusion: The packed recursive-family surface certificate holds by aggregation over the boundary, catalog, and characterization modules.

files.summary: This file turns the recursive-family escape surfaces into one exact three-route finite catalog. It defines projection-or-DP, nonlinear-out-of-class, and ablation routes with length, nodup, and completeness lemmas. It packages boundary-lifted catalogs and proves every orienting KO7 direct observer lands in one of the three routes via the existing trichotomy. It claims no converse beyond the formalized class.
files.conclusion: Every orienting KO7 direct observer lands in one of the three exact recursive-family escape routes.

files.summary: This file gives the schema-generic half of escape-route characterization. It defines a four-clause escape disjunction over exposure, pump, visibility, and sensitivity failures. It proves by classical case-split that any globally orienting observer must fall into a clause, using the unconditional barrier theorem. It packages this as a certificate available for every duplicating family, with the converse deferred to KO7.
files.conclusion: Every duplicating family admits the one-way classification from orienting observers to failure of a DWO precondition.

files.summary: This file catalogues existing typed, many-sorted, and policy-indexed claims as seven named rows. It records per-row projection witnesses onto existing theorem-backed identifiers without reopening proofs. It proves the seven-row catalog exact and every projection holds by reusing substrate theorems. It closes with a marker conjoining completeness and projection.
files.conclusion: All seven typed and policy rows project onto existing theorem-backed substrate surfaces with an exact complete catalog.

files.summary: This file isolates the minimum honest interface for a single rewrite rule whose right side duplicates a distinguished payload variable, with term, coordinate and position types plus occurrence data. It requires one lhs occurrence and at least two rhs occurrences plus a declared closed-firability proposition that is metadata only. It proves the duplication gap is at least one, the rhs count strictly exceeds the lhs count, and the rhs count is positive.
files.conclusion: Any right-duplicating schema has strictly larger rhs payload count with a duplication gap of at least one.

files.summary: This file embeds each right-duplicating schema with base and step traces into an RDRS recursive family and lifts the family boundary predicate to schemas. It proves unconditionally that every schema lies outside the uniform-cost direct-measure orientation boundary and that every schema orbit is mass-indistinguishable from any circular-reference orbit. It provides a barrier catalog carrier with empty and list constructors, size and a membership corollary for downstream extensions.
files.conclusion: Every right-duplicating recursor schema is outside the uniform-cost direct-measure orientation boundary.

files.summary: This file is a reach test for the Phase F.5 escape-route characterization pair, checking by #check that every public name from the schema-generic and KO7 instantiation layers type-checks. It defines a private minimal duplicating schema over Bool and Unit and a private duplicating family over that schema with a false-to-true step. It then shows by example that the schema-generic escape certificate applies to the inline family and that a constant Nat orienter matches the KO7 nat direct orienter scalar.
files.conclusion: All Phase F.5 escape-route names type-check and the schema-generic certificate applies unconditionally to the inline duplicating family.

files.summary: This file checks the eleven-row recursive-family boundary closeout catalog. It verifies resolvability of the row type, catalog list, completeness certificate and per-row projection predicate. Five examples replay length, universal projection, the bundled closeout marker, membership and one concrete-row projection.
files.conclusion: The eleven-row recursive-family boundary closeout catalog is complete with every row projecting to a theorem-backed surface.

files.summary: This file checks that the right-duplicating recursor schema and duplicating recursive-family shells elaborate. Examples confirm the structures, gap constants, payload-count strictness and gap lower bounds resolve. The header states the file does not prove the eventual recursive-family boundary theorem.
files.conclusion: The recursor schema and recursive-family shells elaborate with their payload-count and gap inequalities.

files.summary: This file checks the recursive-family surface-closeout certificate and its marker theorem. It verifies the closed structure, the surface-closed theorem and the module anchor. Three examples replay the three-row escape count, boundary-catalog size preservation and boundary-lift routes.
files.conclusion: The recursive-family surface certificate projects the expected escape-catalog counts, sizes and routes.

files.summary: This file checks the exact recursive-family escape catalog surface and its boundary lift. It covers routes, row length, uniqueness and completeness, the catalog structure and the exhaustive characterization derived from the escape trichotomy. Two examples replay membership and the boundary-lift route identity.
files.conclusion: The three-route recursive-family escape catalog is length-exact, duplicate-free, complete and exhaustive via the escape trichotomy.

files.summary: This file checks the seven-row typed and policy catalog for recursive families. It verifies the row type, list, completeness certificate and per-row projection predicate. Examples replay every row projection in turn and the bundled Phase E-prime closeout marker. The module transitively pulls all substrate modules.
files.conclusion: All seven typed-policy rows project to existing substrate surfaces with the Phase E-prime closeout holding.

files.summary: This file checks reachability of the right-duplicating schema-barrier module. It runs #check for schema-to-family maps, outside-boundary predicates, the unconditional theorem, orbit indistinguishability and the barrier catalog with size lemmas. Four examples instantiate empty and list-built catalogs, the headline universal theorem as a value, and the zero size.
files.conclusion: All right-duplicating schemas are unconditionally outside the boundary with circular orbit indistinguishability.

claims.heading: Full arctic-class split following Cor. 5.11
claims.reason: Finite-diagonal blockedness forces nonfiniteness for strict orientation, while the two non-universality theorems provide orienting and non-orienting one-coordinate models, packaged by the exact split.

claims.heading: Thm. 5.22 (pump-free)
claims.reason: Two trichotomies give the pump-free case split and pumpFree_of_withPump gives containment of the pumped universe. No single theorem gives both trichotomy and containment.

claims.paper: The Orientation Boundary for Step-Duplicating Recursors: A Machine-Checked Structural Theory of Termination Proofs
claims.heading: Thm. 5.22
claims.reason: The schema trichotomy covers every schema, the extended KO7 trichotomy adds the CWS head-precedence universe, and the leaves-universe theorem gives the unconditional third disjunct over the 13-family inductive. Together they cover the full escape claim.

claims.reason: The theorem says any directly orienting KO7 orienter is not barrier-representable, i.e. outside the twelve-family universe.
